input.brief: Open-source code-first headless CMS that installs inside a Next.js app; schema in TypeScript, polished admin for editors

direction.name: The product performs
direction.idea: Software is most convincing when it is doing its job in front of you. Instead of describing features, put small, true, working fragments of the product on the page: the actual control, with real content, responding to the pointer. A colour picker's loupe reads the page's own background and prints its value. A list tool lets you tick an item right there. A type-scale plugin sets the page's own headings. Find the one interaction that is the product and make the hero that interaction; then show each further capability as another fragment at real size. No dashboard collage, no browser frame, no screenshots shrunk until unreadable.
direction.composition: Hero: a short plain headline (4–6vw, left-aligned, upper-left third) and one sentence; the rest of the first screen is the main fragment at actual interface size, sitting directly on the page or on one flat stage colour, large enough to read every label. The fragment is built in HTML and works. Below, capabilities are a single-column sequence, each a row of two parts on a 5/7 split: a two-line statement on one side and the relevant fragment on the other, with the fragments varying in size and shape so the column never becomes a zigzag of equal blocks. Fragments are cropped pieces of interface (a menu, a row, a control, a panel edge), not whole windows. One section pins a fragment while three short statements change it.
direction.typography: The marketing type matches the product's interface type so the fragments and the page feel like one thing. Headline modest; interface text at its true size (13–15px) inside fragments.
direction.colour: Neutral ground. The product's own interface colours provide the colour. At most one flat stage colour behind fragments.
direction.imagery: The interface fragments are the main imagery: build them carefully with real labels, real numbers and sensible states (one hovered, one selected). Around them, two or three real pictures of the customer's world (found with scripts/assets.mjs), never stock of people at laptops.
direction.richness: Fidelity. A fragment with believable content and a real hover state is more interesting than any illustration. Spend the effort there.
direction.pitfalls: A fake interface made of grey bars and circles is the worst outcome; if you cannot build a believable fragment, change direction. Mark each fragment's root element with the attribute data-ui: inside it the product's own conventions apply (1px control borders, small radii, a shadow on its open menu) and the inspector leaves them alone; outside it the house rules hold as usual. data-ui is for cropped fragments only, never for a page wrapper. Do not put the fragment in a browser or laptop frame.

hero.name: Control that reads the page
hero.blueprint: A near-black or deep neutral ground split into two halves by tone alone: the right half is one step lighter than the left, and they meet at a clean vertical edge at 50%. Left half: a small logo mark top-left at a 40px margin, then two-thirds of empty ground, then everything else anchored bottom-left, 40px from the edges: a one-line headline at clamp(26px, 2.1vw, 32px) in medium weight, one supporting sentence at 17px in the softer ink held to 44ch, and the single action as a light rectangular button. Right half: one fragment of the product, centred, about 450px square, built in HTML and working. It is the product's defining control (a loupe, a picker, a dial, a field) and it acts on the page itself: it reads the real background colour, the real headline size or the pointer position and prints that value in its own readout at 13px. Mark its root with data-ui so the product's own radii and borders apply inside it. There is no navigation bar; one text link sits top-right at 15px.
hero.mobile: The halves stack as two tones. The fragment comes first: 78vw square, centred in the lighter block, which is 58svh tall, still live and reading the page under the visitor's finger. The darker block below holds the headline at 6.4vw on up to two lines, the sentence at 16px and the button, left-aligned at 20px. The logo mark sits top-left over the first block.
hero.headline: One plain line at 26–32px naming what the tool is, up to about 32 characters, wrapping to two lines on a phone.

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Headline you can type
sections.blueprint: The section's headline is an input. One line at clamp(48px, 8vw, 132px), tight tracking, flush left across columns 1–12, is a real `<input>` (root marked data-ui) with no border and no fill, prefilled with a believable two-to-five-word example of what a user gives the product: a search, a question, a date in words, a colour name. A solid caret block 0.08em wide blinks after the last character. 48px beneath, on the same left edge, the product's answer appears at true interface size, at most 560px wide: three result rows, one parsed value, or a swatch, updating as the visitor types. Bottom-left, three more examples at 17px act as plain text buttons that refill the line. The rest of the 88svh field is empty. If the text outgrows the line it scrolls inside the input; it never wraps.
sections.mobile: The input is set at 11vw on one line and scrolls sideways inside itself when the text runs long. The answer follows 28px below at full width and true size. The three examples become a wrapping row of filled blocks 44px tall beneath the answer; tapping one refills the line.

sections.name: Fixed output, live controls
sections.blueprint: A split the reader operates. Left, columns 1–6: a flat colour field that is position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh, edge to edge, holding one thing the product makes (a card, an email, a chart, a rendered page) centred at true size, about 420px wide, root marked data-ui. Right, columns 8–12: a reading column no wider than 44ch, with four or five capability blocks 50vh apart. Each block is a sentence at 28–32px, a paragraph at 17px, and directly beneath it one real control at interface size: a slider, a segmented choice, a toggle, a short text field. Operating a control changes the fixed output on the left at once, and changes persist, so by the last block the reader has configured their own. The section heading, two to four words at 40–44px, opens the right column, 72px from the top.
sections.mobile: The output sits in a sticky field at the top, 42svh tall, cropped to its most telling region, not shrunk. Blocks scroll beneath on the page ground: sentence at 22px, paragraph at 16px, control at full width with 44px targets. The field releases after the last block.

sections.name: One card, four fields
sections.blueprint: Four flat colour fields stand side by side across the full viewport, each 25vw wide and 84svh tall, butted together with no gaps; neighbours differ clearly in lightness. The same card from the product (a ticket, an order, a request) appears once in each field at the same height, 38% down, centred, 260px wide at true size, each copy marked data-ui. It is further along every time: bare as it arrives, then with an owner and a due date, then with its checklist half ticked, then closed with its final figure. Along the bottom of each field, 28px in, one clause at clamp(22px, 2vw, 32px) on two lines begins with its order word: 'First it lands here.' 'Then someone takes it.' The heading, two to four words at the same size in the heaviest weight, sits top-left in the first field only. On hover a field's card rises 6px over 150ms.
sections.mobile: The fields stack, each full width and 64svh tall, colours meeting edge to edge. In each: the clause at 24px top-left with 20px margins, then the card at true size, left-aligned, 32px below. The heading sits in the first field above its clause, at 24px in the heaviest weight.

sections.name: Two-ended rows, narrow column
sections.blueprint: A list in one narrow column, 520px wide, starting at 22% of the viewport width or centred. Every row is 34–38px tall with no box and nothing drawn between rows. Each row has two ends: at the left, a 16px round image (a face, a logo, a colour dot) followed after 8px by the name at 15–16px in full ink; at the far right of the column, a short value at 13px in the soft ink (a date, a price, a domain, an opening time) with tabular figures. Entries that need a sentence run to two lines at the left, and the value aligns with the first line. Groups are separated by 40px of space and begin with one plain word in the soft ink at the same size. A heading of two to four words at 24–28px in medium weight sits 32px above the first row. Holds 10–40 rows.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Rows are 44px tall for touch; the left image stays 16px. Long values wrap beneath the name at 13px, left-aligned with it, and the row grows. Group spacing is 32px.

sections.name: First step, already open
sections.blueprint: The page ends with the product's first screen already open. A full-bleed field in the accent colour, 90svh tall. Right, in columns 7–11, vertically centred: the product's own create dialog at true size, 440px wide, root marked data-ui, with its real title ('Name your workspace'), one text field holding an editable, believable example, one two-option segmented choice and its primary button. Inside the fragment the product's conventions apply, including the shadow its dialog normally casts. The field accepts typing, the choice switches, and the primary button is the page's only action: it carries the typed value into sign-up. Left, in columns 1–5, anchored to the bottom with 40px margins: the closing line, two to four words at clamp(56px, 7vw, 112px), leading 0.92, on two lines, and under it one sentence at 17px saying what happens after the button. The upper-left stays empty.
sections.mobile: The closing line leads at 13vw on two lines, top-left, with its sentence beneath at 16px. The dialog follows at full width inside 16px margins, at true size, its primary button 52px tall and full width. The field is at least 84svh; the dialog sits in its lower half.

sections.name: A footer of tiles
sections.blueprint: The footer is the last two rows of a board: filled tiles with 8px gaps and 8–12px outer margins, every cell used. Upper row, each tile 220px tall: a statement tile in columns 1–4 with one sentence at 24px top-left and the legal text at 12px bottom-left; a navigation tile in columns 5–7 with a plain list at 16px; a tile in columns 8–9 giving the city and local time as text; an email tile in columns 10–12 with the address at 20px as a link, bottom-left. Lower row, 320px tall: a tile in the ink colour spanning columns 1–8 with the wordmark set large (about 9vw) and centred, and a tile in the accent colour in columns 9–12 with a two-to-four-word invitation top-left at 28px and an arrow, drawn as inline SVG with 4px strokes, in its bottom-right corner; the whole accent tile is a link.
sections.mobile: Two columns of tiles with 6px gaps: the wordmark tile full width first at 160px tall, the accent tile full width next, then navigation and email side by side, then time and statement. Every tile keeps 20px padding and top-left text.

references.name: Shelf
references.idea: Saves scattered across a dozen places are funnelled into one searchable shelf, shown literally by tumbling source chips and a panel edge that narrows to a point.
references.hero: An off-white panel sits inside a 12px warm-grey page frame. A compact floating nav about 880px wide: logo left, three links and a lime waitlist button right. Centred stack: a small grey pill badge with a sparkle icon, then a two-line headline in General Sans Semibold at about 5.8vw with tight tracking, one word of which sits on a lime rounded-rectangle highlight; a two-line grey subhead; an email field with its button nested inside one rounded outline, 460px wide. From 75% down, the top of a bordered app window rises, and a larger search bar holding a half-typed query overlaps it with a soft shadow.
references.type: General Sans Semibold for headings (84px hero, 40 to 50px section heads, -0.03em); Switzer for everything else at 14 to 20px, mostly mid-grey. About four sizes. The one flourish is a headline word set on a coloured block.
references.colour: #fbfbf9 #f2f1ed #1b1b19 #9ee86f #e9e9e6 — Warm off-whites and soft charcoal with one lime green: the nav button, the highlighted word, small tags and a full-colour closing block.
references.imagery: Vector mock-ups of the app: a bordered window with sidebar and save cards, an enlarged search field, tiny wireframe thumbnails in step cards. No photography. Angled pill chips with small source icons act as illustration.
references.layout: Centred column inside large rounded off-white panels separated by the grey page frame. Mostly stacked heading-plus-subtext blocks, one left and right split, one narrow accordion column. Panel edges are shaped: one ends in a shallow downward chevron.

sections.description: A centred heading and two-line subtext are partly covered by about nine grey pill chips, each naming a save source with a small icon, rotated at random angles as if dropped. The panel's bottom edge is a shallow V pointing down at centre; from its tip a thin vertical line descends about 80px to a second centred heading, subtext and an empty search field, so the layout itself draws a funnel.

A rounded white panel split in two. Left, from a 10% inset: a small lime tag with icon, a two-line heading at about 50px and two short grey paragraphs, vertically centred. Right, from 53% to 90%: three stacked rounded grey cards about 130px tall, each with a white thumbnail tile at left (a tiny wireframe or the logo) and at right a black numbered dot, a bold one-line title and a line or two of grey text.

A lime rounded block about two-thirds of the width, flanked by narrower lime blocks at left and right separated by 14px gaps, as if cropped from a row. Inside, left-aligned and vertically centred: a 40px heading, two lines of small text and a white email field with the button nested in it. A one-line footer sits on a white strip below.

steal: Shape a section's bottom edge into a chevron and run a hairline from its tip to the next heading, turning 'many into one' into layout.
Overlap an enlarged, half-typed search field onto the product window so the hero shows the key interaction rather than a whole screenshot.
Frame the page as rounded panels inside a slightly darker margin so sections read as stacked sheets.

references.name: Dabbit
references.idea: The colour picker demonstrates itself on the page: its loupe sits in the hero reading the site's own background hex, and every feature is shown as a real fragment of the app.
references.hero: Near-black viewport split exactly in half by a one-pixel vertical hairline. Left half: a small chrome four-petal logo top-left at a 40px margin, then two thirds of empty dark, then everything else anchored bottom-left: a one-line 30px medium-weight headline, three lines of grey 18px copy, a light pill button beside an outlined pill, and a tiny note. Right half: a 450px rounded square with a thin iridescent border, the app's loupe, empty except for a centre crosshair dot and a small chip reading the hex of the page's own background. Eight pastel dots and lozenges drift across the top-right like spilled swatches.
references.type: InterVariable only. Headline a modest 30px medium with -0.025em tracking; section heads about 22px; cell titles 15px; body 16px grey. Largest text is 3.3vw. Hierarchy comes from white against grey rather than size; hex values use tabular figures.
references.colour: #141416 #2b2b2e #f4f3f2 #9a9aa0 #f4a48c #d4c6e6 — Charcoal ground, off-white and grey text, no brand accent. All colour comes from the product: pastel swatches, tonal scales, and a thin prismatic edge on the loupe and logo. Neutral-cool.
references.imagery: Live-drawn UI fragments on canvas: swatch strips, eleven-step scales, contrast tables, a Figma plugin panel, each in a slightly lighter rounded panel. A chrome 3D logo and chrome price numerals are the only non-UI images.
references.layout: 40px outer margins; the hero's centre hairline becomes a three-column then four-column hairline grid. No section changes background; rhythm is small eyebrow, heading, grid, repeat. Text sits top-left in every cell.

sections.description: A three-column grid ruled by one-pixel hairlines with no card backgrounds. Each cell is over 400px tall: 15px white title and three lines of grey copy, plus a real UI fragment docked above or below (a swatch history strip, a tonal scale, a contrast table, a ten-by-ten colour matrix). Rows alternate text-over-mock and mock-over-text so the grid staggers. The loupe square from the hero reappears floating across cell boundaries.

A four-column, three-row grid of minor features divided by hairlines. Each item is a 14px title prefixed by a tiny coloured glyph (dot, square, triangle or dash, one shape per column, in the app's pastel colours) and two lines of grey text. No icons, no cards, no hover chrome.

Left third: small grey eyebrow, a 22px heading, one paragraph. Right: the price rendered as huge chrome 3D numerals about 150px tall with the loupe square overlapping them, a tiny qualifier beside, and a plain four-line checklist beneath. No pricing card, no border, no tiers.

Closing block centred on the same dark ground: the chrome four-petal logo enlarged to about 200px, pastel shapes scattered widely around it, a two-line 22px sentence, the same two pill buttons, then a one-line footer with copyright left and seven text links right.

steal: Make the hero demo sample the page itself: the tool reports the site's own background value, proving the product without a screenshot.
Build feature grids from hairlines and real UI fragments instead of bordered cards and icons, alternating text-above and mock-above per row.
Keep the headline small (30px) and anchored bottom-left so the product object, not the slogan, owns the first viewport.

references.name: Textmode Overlay
references.idea: The whole site is rendered in the product's medium: one bitmap face and live character-art fields, laid out like a terminal instrument panel with a numbered rail.
references.hero: Black viewport framed like an instrument panel. A 60px top bar with a hairline beneath: wordmark and version left, four small caps links right, a cream block button filling the bar's right end. A narrow right-edge rail lists 01 to 10 vertically; the active number extends leftward as an outlined label tab. The main area is a canvas of dim grey character marks with a few red ones, small caps captions in its top corners. The headline, two lines of cream pixel caps at 11vw, is left-aligned at mid-height, its last word in a slanted variant. Below a hairline, a bottom strip holds a short description left and two wide rectangular buttons.
references.type: Monogram Extended, a bitmap face, for 96% of text: 160px headline caps, 24px body, small caps labels, one weight, with a slanted variant for the accent word. Inter appears only in the cookie dialog. Hierarchy comes from size and case alone.
references.colour: #0a0a0a #f2f2ec #3b3b3b #b11226 #9a9a95 — Black with cream text and mid-grey glyph texture. Deep crimson appears as scattered characters, soft radial glows behind panels and slider fills. The last two sections invert to cream with black type.
references.imagery: Live canvas renderings: a swirling white, grey and red brush-stroke animation shown beside its character-art conversion, plus ambient character fields as backgrounds. Square corners, hairline frames, no photographs.
references.layout: Full-width panel grid drawn with 1px lines: 32px margins, a persistent right rail, sections built from bordered cells (three equal columns, a two-by-three spec table beside a wide panel, control strips). Each section starts with a small slash-separated caption and a large caps heading.

sections.description: A wide bordered frame split vertically by a draggable handle: the left half shows the source animation (thick white, grey and crimson swirls on black), the right half the same frame converted to scattered characters, with small outlined tags in the top corners naming each side. Beneath, a control strip of bordered cells offers segmented options (cell size in four steps with the active one filled cream, glyph set, invert, motion), like a hardware panel.

Three equal tall columns divided by hairlines inside one outer frame, each about 300px high. A single caps word sits at mid-left of each column in roughly 36px pixel type and two lines of small text sit at the bottom-left. A soft crimson radial glow is centred behind the middle column and fades into the outer two, the only shading in the section.

Left 40%: a two-by-three table of bordered cells, each with a tiny index number top-left, a caps feature name at mid-left and a small grey quantity bottom-right. Right 60%: one large cell with a two-line caps heading upper-left, a crimson glow in the top-right corner and two lines of description along the bottom. The rail tab at the right edge names the section.

The close inverts to cream: a pale character field with a faint red cluster at upper right, a slash-separated caption, then a two-line black pixel-caps headline at about 8vw that echoes the hero and reuses the slanted last word, and one small outlined rectangular button. Footer links follow in three small columns on the same cream ground.

steal: Add a fixed right-edge rail of section numbers where the active number sprouts a labelled tab into the content area.
Draw the page as bordered cells with 1px lines and put a tiny index top-left and a small quantity bottom-right in each feature cell.
End on an inverted, light-ground repeat of the hero headline so the close mirrors the opening in the opposite palette.
